conventions.convention: A typed state x is represented by JΓ(x)=wΓ e(Γ,x), where wΓ is the positive sum of its primitive amounts. Separated composition adds coefficient maps. Distinct scaled tags are related by reversible preparation transport, not equality of raw point masses.

Accessibility compares equal bookkeeping masses; equal scalar mass does not identify primitive composition. A1–A6 initially impose no comparison hypothesis. Strict comparison means forward accessibility without reverse accessibility.
Simple charts are nonempty open convex subsets of R^(n+1), n≥1. S2 supplies a unique supporting plane with finite, locally Lipschitz slope. S3 concerns the boundary relative to the chart.
Stability removes fixed positive equal-mass spectators along a positive sequence decreasing to zero; the spectator mass need not equal the base mass.

Thermal equivalence means reversibility between a separated pair and its distinct tagged thermal join. T2 additionally requires equal-state splits to be reversible with their joins. Every finite join is assumed to satisfy the simple-domain hypotheses.

T5 quantifies over every ordered system pair, every state in the first system, and every permitted work coordinate in the second. C1 separately relates an equilibrated join to each constituent; coordinate addition alone supplies neither condition.
Signed comparison uses the negative and positive parts of v−u, with equal raw coefficient totals. Signed maps are formal notation; negative coefficients are not physical preparations.
The common energy orientation is an affine mathematical proof-coordinate convention. It preserves the join energy sum and does not redefine physical energy or establish a measured temperature sign.

Decorated chains have finitely many independently specified edges and one common catalyst; adjacent edge output and input states need not coincide. Costs are real witness sums. Their infimum is +∞ without witnesses and −∞ for costs unbounded below; opposite-sign infinite sums are undefined.

Arbitrary-family calibration explicitly assumes Choice and characterizes same-composition comparisons only. Cross-type offset monotonicity additionally assumes no sinks and concludes only a weak inequality.

load_bearing.statement: The represented coefficient-map framework assumes A1–A6 on equal-mass finite compounds, A7 on each simple chart, and S1–S3, without assuming comparison completeness.

Under A1–A6, for equal-mass compounds A,B and every finite spectator C, A+C≺B+C if and only if A≺B. Signed comparison agrees with ordinary comparison on nonnegative maps, is translation invariant, transitive, and additive. No comparison hypothesis is used.

Under the forward-sector hypotheses, each simple domain has a constant fixed-work orientation sign. In positively oriented coordinates its sector boundary is a C1 graph over an open connected work-coordinate projection, with locally Lipschitz derivative Du_x(v)=−P_i(u_x(v),v). If y belongs to the boundary of A_x, then A_y=A_x.

Under the forward-sector hypotheses, sectors are nested; boundary membership gives equal sectors, interior membership gives inclusion in the earlier sector's interior, every two simple states are comparable, and strict comparison is exactly interior membership.

Assume the forward-sector hypotheses and T1–T4 for every finite join. For any one simple type, every two finite compounds of its scaled copies with the same total coefficient mass are comparable. No entropy across different material types is asserted.

For two simple domains in a family of finite thermal joins satisfying A1–A7, S1–S3, T1–T5, and C1, there are strict pairs x0≺≺x1 and y0≺≺y1 with (x0,y1)∼(x1,y0). CH holds for every fixed finite composition of scaled copies of those two types.

For the stated nonempty explicit finite-factor family with distinguished meter, strict meter pair, join-closed calibrator hypotheses, and Choice, additive constants and positive scales can be chosen so that the finite entropy sum is additive, extensive, and characterizes every same-composition comparison. No cross-composition conclusion is asserted.

The decorated cost has F(Γ,Γ)=0, positive homogeneity, catalyst invariance, triangle inequality and composition subadditivity whenever the relevant extended sums are defined. Every actual forward/reverse witness pair has nonnegative total cost; a finite reverse witness bounds all forward costs below.

Under the calibrated entropy family, cross-type A1–A6, and the decorated-cost definition, equal-mass endpoint states satisfy x≺y if and only if σΓ(x)+F(Γ,Γ′)≤σΓ′(y), including unattained infima and the stated infinite-value conventions.

Assuming Choice and no sinks for the decorated cost, there is an additive extensive real type offset B satisfying −F(Γ′,Γ)≤B(Γ)−B(Γ′)≤F(Γ,Γ′). When admitted transitions satisfy the calibrated cost inequality, σΓ(x)+B(Γ) is nondecreasing across them; no-gap equalities and strict extensions are not concluded.

concerns.concern: The displayed item order precedes several suppliers with their consumers: lem-tdmath-forward-spectator-cancellation precedes def-tdmath-forward-signed-comparison; lem-tdmath-reference-strip-coordinate precedes thm-tdmath-sector-nesting; and thm-tdmath-sector-nesting precedes thm-tdmath-forward-boundary-graph. Their actual dependency declarations and proofs require the reverse ordering. This is an exposition-order issue, not a dependency cycle.

alerts.finding: Step 1.2 says '[A3] ... supplies T1–T4 ... and reversible splitting used in [F1]', but the equal-state clause does not match the mathematical supplier. def-tdmath-thermal-contact-hypotheses requires 'the equal-state split of any state into positive scaled copies of itself is reversible' in its join-splitting formulation; lem-tdmath-thermal-scaling-invariance explicitly uses reversibility of the pair with its thermal join. In contrast, post-td-thermal-join-axioms T2 states that '(t x,(1-t)x) is reversible to x.' def-td-thermal-join retains a distinct tagged join with both work coordinates and supplies no identification or reversible comparison between that join and x. A5 likewise relates the split to x. Thus the transfer has not established the equal-state pair-to-join reversibility needed by the mathematical supplier. T1 provides only the forward pair-to-join direction, while the general T2 existence clause supplies some reversible split, not necessarily this equal-state split.

The convex page supplies its global comparison and calibration arguments separately and does not strengthen the Pfaff page's expressly local conclusions.

The physics consumers preserve T5, C1, Choice, represented type weights, same-composition calibration, and weak cross-type monotonicity. However, pthm-td-contact-product-comparison does not establish the mathematical supplier's equal-state pair-to-join reversibility from the physical T2 formulation; see the routed alert. Its downstream calibration consequently inherits this unresolved transfer obligation.
